prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Produce a 3D reconstruction reference for ONE whole mature white daikon radish plant. Crucial correction: its leaf crown must have real ROUND THREE-DIMENSIONAL radial volume, equal front-to-back and left-to-right spread, never a flat fan or botanical herbarium arrangement. Show from an elevated three-quarter viewpoint, approximately 40 degrees downward: clearly show the oval top of the white root shoulder, then EIGHT leaves radiating in distinct compass directions around the top of that root. Two foreground leaves extend TOWARD the viewer in strong foreshortening and curl down, two sideways, two behind with smaller apparent length, and two shorter upright center leaves. Each blade has one broad terminal lobe plus two or three rounded lateral lobes and fine toothed edges, NOT a smooth cabbage leaf; thin leaf surfaces, modest waviness, slender pale-green petioles each joining the same central crown. Root is a clean long cylindrical ivory-white daikon, firm rounded shoulder pale green at the crown, tapering gradually to a small tip. Keep root completely visible, about 45% of plant total height, centered vertical growth axis. Image 1 sets approved gongbi fine-line / light-colour style; image 2 botanical photo defines radial lobed crown anatomy; image 3 actual white root anatomy. Gentle sage/celadon pigments with preserved watercolor mottling, SELECTIVE fine moss-green contours and sparse leaf vein lines, matte dimensional forms. Soft neutral diffuse light, plain neutral-gray backdrop, no ground, no cast shadow, no pot, no soil, no text, no grids, no collage, no photography or rubbery inflated leaves. Leave clear negative space between the eight leaves so their front/back attachment and radial directions are readable. Whole plant and every leaf tip fully inside frame. Do not arrange all leaves in one plane just to show their flat upper surfaces.
